title: GPT 6.1 Terra Pro: Pricing, Speed and Capabilities
summary: GPT 6.1 Terra Pro adds new automation capabilities. Understand which workflow tasks could benefit from this model and how it changes what's automatable.
body_markdown:
## Terra Pro's cost and speed


You **pay about 15 times more per task** for GPT 6.1 Terra Pro than for gpt-5.4-mini on our test, so the gap has to show up in your results.


### Terra Pro price on OpenAI's pricing page


On[OpenAI's pricing page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing) , gpt-5.4-mini is listed at $0.75 input, $0.075 cached input and $4.50 output per million tokens. Its cheaper neighbours on that page were gpt-6.1-terra at $1, $0.05 and $5. The other is gpt-6-luna at $0.10, $0.01 and $0.50.


Because Luna's input rate is 7.5 times below gpt-5.4-mini's, a high-volume classification step may not need either. Gpt-6.1-sol, a current model, was listed at $2, $0.10 and $10, and gpt-5.6-terra at $2, $0.20 and $12, so a "Terra" name does not tell you the tier.


### Cost per task in practice


On our small workflow test, Terra Pro cost $0.0022 per task against $0.000142 for gpt-5.4-mini, over fifteen times as much. Median seconds per task are labelled on each bar.


Read the chart as a price for the whole task, not per token. At 10,000 runs a month, that's about $22 against $1.42, trivial either way, but it scales linearly if you run millions.


When steps chain, the seconds on the bars matter more than the dollars. Latency compounds: a model that is slower on one call is slower on every call in a five-step flow, and the wait lands on whoever is watching the run.


Check the bars against your own timeout settings before you change a model field.
